title: Grove's Limiting Step: Eliminating Task-Switching Thrash
hook: Every system has exactly one constraint that dictates throughput. Everything else is waiting.
core_insight: In 'High Output Management', Andy Grove demonstrates that production must be constructed around the 'limiting step'—the operation with the longest lead time or lowest capacity. For neurodivergent deep work, task-switching incurs catastrophic re-orientation penalties. Identify today's single limiting step, isolate it from all interrupt channels, and clear it before touching ancillary queues.
takeaways: Find the single critical-path constraint before opening client/advisory queues.
Batch interruptions into scheduled buffers; refuse ad-hoc context switches.
external_reference: Andy Grove, High Output Management, Ch. 2
